title: Playing with Kid Punch and Lee Collins on parades
summary: He played trumpet in Punch's band and with Lee Collins on parades, naming the trombone, clarinet and banjo players; parade bands were made up.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, you were talking about, uh, another band you heard, who was that?
No, I used to play with Punch. Oh, yeah, Punch. Kid Punch. I played at Lee Collins on parade, you know. And I played at Punch in the orchestra, you know.
Do you remember who was in Punch's band then?
Yeah. It had, uh, Jack Carey. Oh, yeah. Jack Carey was a trombone player. Georgia Boy on clarinet, Walter Preston on banjo.
Did you play second trumpet or were you playing bass then?

Well, no, I wasn't playing bass then. I was playing trumpet. Trumpet. Trumpet. Yeah. And they had, uh, Eddie Morris was playing trombone. Oh, yeah. Eddie Morris on trombone. That was a six piece band too. Punch was good too in that time. It was fast singing. I used to love a young play. And, uh, I played at Lee Collins a lot of time on parades. Whose band was that?
Do you remember? Was there any special band like Onrigger Tuxedo or one of those organized bands? Or just a makeup band?
Uh, made up band. On the parades, it was made up band. Yeah. It was made up band. Different fellas, you know.
